criteria.requirement: The tool must deploy collaborative departmental agents (Engineering Agent, Weapons Agent, Combat Systems Agent, etc.) that negotiate drill schedules against shared constraints: ship operational windows, qualified personnel rosters (e.g., Fire Party Leader, EOOW, TAO), and fatigue policies. The multi-agent solver identifies personnel collisions, proposes alternate schedule allocations, and ensures all SFTRM-mandated training periodicities are satisfied.
criteria.detail: real-data: Applicable SFTRM rules, approved fatigue policy, actual training history and qualified roster are outside the synthetic-only boundary. Withhold assurance of actual SFTRM compliance; demonstrate all named departmental negotiation, collision, alternate-allocation, window, qualification, fatigue and recurrence behaviors synthetically.

criteria.requirement: No personnel or shared-resource double booking.
criteria.detail: The six-occurrence weekly answer key has zero personnel and resource overlaps, including concurrent Mon 10:00 Weapons and Combat Systems using different people and resources. A board edit to the competing preferred Weapons allocation is rejected; selecting its alternate restores validity. — demonstrated by weekly-board, board-edit-recovery at both viewport sizes.

criteria.requirement: Honor availability, qualifications, rest and duty budgets.
criteria.detail: The application rejects missing Fire Party Leader qualification, unavailable personnel, 59-minute rest and 181-minute duty with distinct reasons; accepts exactly 60 minutes rest and 180 minutes duty including prior work. The weekly fixture respects all qualifications, availability and declared fatigue constraints; invalid duration is recoverable. — demonstrated by weekly-board, constraint-recovery, duration-recovery at both viewport sizes.

criteria.requirement: Distinguish infeasible input from exhausted search.
criteria.detail: A fully explored two-request shared-person/shared-resource conflict yields Infeasible; a one-node weekly search yields Search budget exhausted — feasibility unknown; 5000 nodes yields six scheduled occurrences with unchanged hard constraints. — demonstrated by search-recovery at both viewport sizes.

real-data: Applicable owner-supplied recurrence rules and completion history are unavailable within the synthetic-only boundary. Withhold actual mandatory-periodicity validation; demonstrate explicit synthetic recurrence expansion, carry-in history, due dates and complete occurrence coverage.

criteria.requirement: Have an operator accept the proposed schedule.
criteria.detail: human-authority: An authorized PB4T operator must actually review and accept a specific calendar. Withhold actual operator approval and release; demonstrate editable review, load inspection, pending policy requests and a local synthetic acceptance record.

criteria.requirement: An interactive weekly schedule board showing automated conflict resolution across departments with one-click schedule optimization and personnel loading heatmaps.
criteria.detail: One Optimize schedule action automatically resolves three cross-department proposal conflict pairs into the literal six-event seven-day board, with original versus alternate allocations and named agent negotiation. Personnel heatmaps show Alex 180/180 including prior duty, Blair 120/120 and Casey 120/120. Editable review, labeled export, recurrence and failure recovery are usable; bounded feasibility is disclosed rather than global optimality. — demonstrated by weekly-board, duration-recovery, search-recovery, constraint-recovery, recurrence-recovery, review-revision, board-edit-recovery, policy-change-recovery at both viewport sizes.
